sections.title: Research Experience Course in Health Psychology: Mind, Body, and Behavior: Exploring the Foundations
sections.description: This research experience course introduces undergraduate students to health psychology, examining how psychological, behavioral, and social factors influence health and illness. Students will explore key topics such as stress and coping, health behavior change, the mind–body connection, and trauma’s connection to chronic illness. We will also study health behaviors such as exercise, sleep, eating, and substance use. We will explore how psychological concepts and research can be applied to health promotion and illness prevention. Additionally, this course offers an informal introduction to research design by including a hands-on experience in designing, conducting, and reporting a piece of psychological research. This objective will be met principally through participation in a group research project, class discussions related to the project and various exercises focusing on individual components of the research process. This class will help you critically evaluate primary research articles. These goals will all be met through lectures, class discussions, group project, exercises, and readings.
